name: Ursa Major: the stars don't move

u4.say: The monks on Enceladus — their geyser hymns. I always took them for noise, but the cadence... it's structured. Line lengths, repeated headers. Take the survey data to them. Tell them the sky held still.

u1b.say: Right. Right. Parallax: when you move, near stars should shift against far ones. It is geometry. It is the LAW.

u6.say: Whatever they sing back to you — that's the half of the proof we couldn't read. Go. And traveler... thank you for looking up with us.

u2.say: Nothing moved. Not one star. Not by a hair. We crossed half the system and the sky did not notice. The stars are not far away, traveler — they are PAINTED. A... a backdrop. A skybox.

options.label: Calm
options.text: Then we're the first people to ever really look. That's not nothing.

options.label: Blunt
options.text: So the sky is fake. What's behind it?

u1.say: You came back. Good. Close the door. ...We finished the parallax survey last night. Twelve years of baselines, every outpost, both solstices.

u3cold.say: Behind it? BEHIND it? Forty years staring up and you ask what's behind the— ...I don't know. Nobody knows. That's the worst part.

u5ask.say: The Curator eyes the rigging bag on your shoulder. 'The high scope hasn't been climbed since the sky froze. Old knees,' he admits.

options.label: Rig
options.text: Leave your Low-G Pitons rigged on the high scope
